title: Consistency compounds
summary: What training for distance and shipping software have in common.

body: I am not a fast runner. What I have become, this year, is a consistent one: between January and September I ran outdoors in 35 of 36 weeks, with an unbroken streak of 33.
Consistency is not dramatic, which is exactly why it works. No single run in that streak mattered much. Together they changed the numbers in a way no single hard session could have.

items.title: 5K
items.detail: My first recorded 5K effort in January took just over an hour. By June the best effort was 38:51.

items.title: Volume
items.detail: Monthly distance built from 41 km in January to a peak of 93 km in April.

items.title: Distance
items.detail: The first 10K came in March, and a half marathon in September.

body: It is the same pattern I see in engineering. A codebase, a data platform or a skill improves through small, repeated, measured steps: input, process, iterate, progress. Skipping a week rarely breaks anything. Skipping the habit breaks everything.
So the goal for the next season is not a time. It is the next week, and the one after that.
